metadata.title: Which educational approaches predict students’ generative AI confidence and responsibility?

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study used an online student survey administered in 15 upper secondary schools in the German-speaking part of Switzerland (penultimate year students), with voluntary participation. The manuscript reports data cleaning (removing 72 respondents who completed the questionnaire in under 5 minutes) and exclusions of classes with fewer than five participants, but it does not report the use of complex survey weights or any sampling/replicate-weight variables. Because the analysis is based on multilevel multiple regression with class-level grouping and does not mention applying survey weights (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) or replicate-weight procedures (e.g., BRR/jackknife), weighting strategy is unclear and likely not applied. The multilevel structure is handled via a hierarchical regression approach (random intercepts at the class level), but no additional weight-based population representativeness adjustments are described.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values are not applicable because the dependent variables (GenAI confidence and GenAI responsibility) are Likert-scale survey constructs derived from factor-validated item scales, not cognitive achievement scores generated via PV-based ILSA scaling. Missing data handling is reported as default listwise exclusion for each multilevel regression model, so no PV/missing-data transparency gap exists for the survey outcomes.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Online survey on Unipark administered between end of November 2023 and March 2024 in 15 upper secondary schools (5 vocational, 5 general baccalaureate, 5 specialized baccalaureate) in the German-speaking part of Switzerland. Students were invited via school leaders to all students enrolled in the penultimate year; participation was voluntary. Data cleaning removed 72 students (3% of respondents) who completed the questionnaire too quickly (<5 minutes). For the multilevel regression, missing data were handled via default listwise exclusion per model, and 47 classes with fewer than five participants (24% of participating classes) were excluded. The final analytic sample used for the regression comprised N=1157 participants across 152 classes.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2022 (not used); Switzerland upper secondary student GenAI survey (2023-2024), multilevel regression
main_findings.performance_metrics: Multilevel multiple regression (class-level random intercept). Model 0 ICC=0.07. Model fit: R2 marginal 0.06 (Model 1) vs 0.09 (Model 2); R2 conditional 0.11 (Model 1) vs 0.13 (Model 2). Model 2 vs Model 1 likelihood ratio test: p<.001. Key effects in Model 2: critical-reflective β=0.11 (p<.001); creative-productive β=0.08 (p<.01); female vs male β=-0.24 (p<.001).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using the Switzerland upper secondary student GenAI survey data (2023-2024) with multilevel multiple regression, the study leveraged Critical-reflective GenAI approach, Creative-productive GenAI approach, and Gender (male/female/other) to predict GenAI confidence, finding that critical-reflective and creative-productive approaches were significant positive predictors while protective-preventive was not significant. This indicates that implementing critical-reflective and, to a lesser extent, creative-productive GenAI media literacy practices may strengthen students’ confidence in understanding and using GenAI, though the cross-sectional design limits causal claims.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2022 (not used); Switzerland upper secondary student GenAI survey (2023-2024), multilevel regression
main_findings.performance_metrics: Multilevel multiple regression (class-level random intercept). Model 0 ICC=0.05. Model fit: R2 marginal 0.02 (Model 1) vs 0.05 (Model 2); R2 conditional 0.10 (Model 1) vs 0.11 (Model 2). Model 2 vs Model 1 likelihood ratio test: p<.001. Key effects in Model 2: critical-reflective β=0.16 (p<.001); protective-preventive not significant; female vs male β=0.09 (p<.01).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using the Switzerland upper secondary student GenAI survey data (2023-2024) with multilevel multiple regression, the study leveraged Critical-reflective GenAI approach, Gender (male/female/other), and Protective-preventive GenAI approach to predict GenAI responsibility, finding that critical-reflective approach was a significant positive predictor while protective-preventive was not significant. This indicates that emphasizing critical evaluation of GenAI outputs and ethical/long-term reflection in everyday classroom practice may foster stronger responsibility beliefs, though causality cannot be inferred from the cross-sectional survey.

data.outcome_summary: This exploratory survey study collected student-reported experiences of three GenAI media literacy education approaches (protective-preventive, critical-reflective, creative-productive) and measured two outcomes—GenAI confidence and GenAI responsibility—among 1157 upper secondary students in 15 highly digitized Swiss schools (German-speaking Switzerland). Using hierarchical multilevel multiple regression with class-level grouping, the authors found that the critical-reflective approach significantly predicted both outcomes (confidence β=0.11, p<.001; responsibility β=0.16, p<.001), while the protective-preventive approach did not significantly predict either outcome. The creative-productive approach predicted GenAI confidence only (β=0.08, p<.01). Model fit improved from Model 1 to Model 2 in both cases (confidence marginal R2 0.06→0.09; responsibility 0.02→0.05), with likelihood ratio tests p<.001. Limitations include self-report measures, listwise exclusion for missing data, collapsed school/class variance due to only 15 schools, and cross-sectional associations rather than causal effects.
